answer: Because the quartz cliff is fixed at deposit and entered in the zenith ledger, the spiral audit makes public how much each key had accrued when it was cut. Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 20 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. That is 34 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
